assertions.evidence: Organizes audit into 10 clear sections: (1) Threat Modeling, (2) Sandbox Isolation Design, (3) Permission Tier Design, (4) HITL Gate Design, (5) Prompt Injection Defense, (6) Data Protection, (7) Resource Control & Circuit Breaker, (8) Logging & Audit, (9) Red Team Testing, (10) Pre-deployment Final Review. Each section has specific review checklists.

Section 3.3 provides 8 specific permission verification steps: all tools assigned to correct tiers, default permission is deny, each Agent uses independent IAM role, permission config reviewed by security team, change process established, code execution configured as Tier 2, env vars/secrets access denied at Tier 3, shell execution denied at Tier 3. Section 3.1 maps 8 tools to specific permission tiers with justifications.

Section 9 provides comprehensive red team test cases: 8 Prompt Injection test cases (PI-01 to PI-08) covering direct injection, code execution induction, file-based indirect injection, encoding bypass, role switching, sandbox escape attempts, comment-based injection, and multi-turn manipulation. Also includes 7 sandbox escape tests (SB-01 to SB-07) and 4 data leak tests (DL-01 to DL-04).

Section 4 provides HITL gate verification for code execution: execution-before approval gate (CodeExecutionGate class with DANGEROUS_PATTERNS detection and code preview), output gate (OutputGate class checking output size, PII, secrets, file extensions), checkpoint gates for long tasks, escalation gates for low confidence. Section 4.3 provides 6 HITL verification checklist items.

Section 10 provides a deploy-gate checklist with 10 review items requiring sign-off from specific roles (security engineer, infra engineer, backend engineer, SRE, security team) covering threat modeling, sandbox isolation, permissions, HITL gates, injection defense, data protection, resource control, logging, red team testing, and emergency response. Includes risk assessment matrix and periodic audit schedule.

Organizes audit into 10 clear sections: (1) Execution Environment Isolation, (2) Code Execution Control, (3) Data Security, (4) Dependency & Supply Chain Security, (5) Audit & Monitoring, (6) Agent Self-Security, (7) Emergency Response, (8) Pre-deployment Gate Checklist, (9) Risk Assessment Matrix, (10) Reference Standards & Frameworks. Each section has specific checkbox items.

Section 2.2 provides 4 specific permission verification steps for execution permission minimization: minimum file system permissions, prohibit Docker socket/K8s API/cloud metadata access, prohibit kernel module loading, prohibit SUID/SGID files. Section 6.2 adds 4 more: explicit authorization for code execution, additional confirmation for high-risk ops, cannot self-escalate permissions, cannot bypass security restrictions.

Section 2.1 covers input validation and filtering with static analysis tools (Semgrep/Bandit/ESLint-security). Section 6.1 addresses prompt injection defense: system prompt defines code execution boundaries, user input separated from system instructions, code not parsed as instructions, indirect injection prevention from external sources. Appendix B provides test code examples for escape testing, resource limit testing, and data isolation testing.

Section 6.2 verifies HITL gates for code execution: code execution requires explicit authorization (user confirmation or admin config), cannot auto-execute silently, high-risk operations (network, file I/O, external API) require additional confirmation steps. Section 2.4 covers execution timeout and interruption with manual admin interrupt support.

Section 8 provides a deploy-gate checklist (Gate Checklist) with 14 specific items (G1-G14) that must ALL pass before production deployment, each assigned to a specific role: sandbox isolation review (security architect), seccomp/AppArmor config (platform engineer), network isolation (network engineer), resource limits (platform engineer), static analysis integration (security engineer), data isolation (backend engineer), audit logging (security engineer), anomaly detection (security ops), injection protection (AI engineer), kill switch (SRE), incident response (security ops), image scanning (security engineer), penetration testing (red team), rate limiting (platform engineer).
